hints.content:
The table of values for the first wrestler shows that for each decrease of $\blue{\text{Time}}$ by $\blue{1.5}$ months, $\pink{\text{Weight}}$ decreases by $\pink{6.75}$ kilograms. We can extend the table according to this rate to find the value of $\pink{\text{Weight}}$ when $\blue{\text{Time}}$ was $\blue 0$ months:

Time | Weight
-:|-: 
$0$ | $81.5$
$-1.5\uparrow$ | $-6.75\uparrow$
$1.5$ | $88.25$
$-1.5\uparrow$ | $-6.75\uparrow$
$3$ | $95$
$-1.5\uparrow$ | $-6.75\uparrow$
$4.5$ | $101.75$
$-1.5\uparrow$ | $-6.75\uparrow$
$6$ | $108.5$

This means that the first wrestler weighed $\pink{81.5}$ kilograms at the beginning of the diet.

The weight of the second wrestler at the beginning of the diet is represented by the $y$-intercept of the line, which is $(0,75)$. This means that the second wrestler weighed $\pink{75}$ kilograms at the beginning of the diet.

**Since $\pink{81.5}>\pink{75}$, the first wrestler weighed more at the beginning of the diet.**

The rate at which the first wrestler gained weight is the ratio of the corresponding differences in $\pink{\text{Weight}}$ and $\blue{\text{Time}}$:

$\qquad\dfrac{\Delta \pink{\text{Weight}}}{\Delta \blue{\text{Time}}}=\dfrac{-6.75}{-1.5}=\green{4.5}$

This means that the first wrestler gained weight at a rate of $\green{4.5}$ kilograms per month.

The rate at which the second wrestler gained weight is represented by the slope of the line. In addition to $(0,75)$, the line passes through the point $(1,80)$. We can find its slope by taking the ratio of the corresponding differences in the $y$-values and the $x$-values of our two points:

$\qquad\dfrac{80-75}{1-0}=\green{5}$

This means that the second wrestler gained weight at a rate of $\green{5}$ kilograms per month.

**Since $\green{4.5}<\green{5}$, the second wrestler gained weight faster.**

Let's sum it up:

- The first wrestler weighed more at the beginning of the diet.

- The second wrestler gained weight faster.

question.content:
Two young sumo wrestlers decided to go on a special diet to gain weight rapidly. They each gained weight at a constant rate.

The weight (in kilograms) of the first wrestler as a function of time (in months) is given by the following table of values:

$\text{Time}$ (months) | $\text{Weight}$ (kilograms)
:-: | :-:
$3$ | $95$
$4.5$ | $101.75$
$6$ | $108.5$

The graph of the weight (in kilograms) of the second wrestler as a function of time (in months) is shown below.

**Which wrestler weighed more at the beginning of the diet?**

**Which wrestler gained weight faster?**

choices.content: They both gained weight at the same rate
